findings: The common name, scientific name, and family are correct: Belted Kingfisher, Megaceryle alcyon, Alcedinidae.

The printed length, wingspan, and weight ranges exactly match the independently checked All About Birds and Audubon pages: 28–35 cm (11.0–13.8 in), 48–58 cm (18.9–22.8 in), and 140–170 g (4.9–6.0 oz).
Every visible prose line and field-mark bullet matches the proposed wording without misspellings, duplicated words, omissions, substitutions, or nonsensical text.

The primary specimen is an anatomically coherent adult female: stocky body, disproportionately large crested head, dark eye, heavy straight pointed bill, blue-gray upperparts, white collar, blue-gray breast band, rusty belly band and flanks, white underparts, spotted wings and tail, and short legs with small orange-gray feet.

The bill is consistently rendered in the primary specimen and detached head study. Both mandibles trace cleanly from a shared base to a pointed, essentially co-terminal tip; no reversed, truncated, or inconsistent projection is present.

The primary specimen has one head, one beak, two normally positioned wings with the far wing naturally occluded, two legs and feet, and one medium-length tail. No duplicated or malformed attached anatomy is present.

The detached spread-wing and head-and-bill studies are clearly separated supplementary illustrations. Their feather structure, wing pattern, crest, eye, collar, and bill proportions are consistent with the species and the supplied field photographs.

The ruler runs upward from 28 cm to 35 cm and has exactly four evenly spaced unlabeled interior ticks, creating five proportional segments. Its endpoints agree with the printed body-length range, and the adjacent label explicitly states that the diagram is schematic and not to scale.

The habitat and behavior text agrees with the checked sources: waterside perching or hovering, headfirst plunge-diving for aquatic prey, loud rattling flight calls, solitary or territorial behavior, and nesting burrows excavated in earthen banks.
The plate has clear hierarchy, balanced spacing, readable typography, a coherent scientific-journal aesthetic, and no overlaps that obscure text or anatomy.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
